top_stories.title: Anthropic cuts off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access following government order
top_stories.summary: Anthropic has cut off access to AI models Fable 5 and Mythos 5 following a government order, in what appears to be a national security-related action. Amazon security research reportedly played a role in prompting the White House to order the ban. The move marks a notable instance of direct government intervention in AI model access.

top_stories.title: A Court Has Ruled That Google Is Liable for False Statements Generated by AI Overviews [Metered]
top_stories.summary: A court has found Google legally liable for false statements produced by its AI Overviews feature, marking a significant legal precedent for AI-generated content. The ruling could have wide-ranging implications for how AI search products are developed and deployed. It raises key questions about publisher and platform responsibility for generative AI outputs.

top_stories.title: Police officer investigated for using AI to 'create evidence' in multiple cases
top_stories.summary: A Derbyshire police officer is under investigation for allegedly using AI to fabricate or manipulate evidence across multiple cases. The case raises serious concerns about AI misuse in law enforcement and the integrity of AI-generated content in legal proceedings. It is thought to be among the first cases of its kind in the UK.

top_stories.title: PwC Report: AI Making Medical Bills Higher
top_stories.summary: A PwC report finds that AI adoption in healthcare is contributing to higher medical bills rather than reducing costs. The report highlights how AI tools are being used in ways that increase billing and administrative charges. The findings challenge the widespread assumption that AI will primarily drive down healthcare costs.

top_stories.title: Rockefeller University Press Collaborates with Cashmere to Enhance Responsible AI Discoverability
top_stories.summary: Rockefeller University Press has announced a collaboration with Cashmere to improve how its academic content is discovered and used responsibly by AI systems. The partnership aims to ensure that AI tools can access and surface peer-reviewed research in an accurate and accountable way. The move reflects growing engagement between academic publishers and AI developers around responsible content use.

further_links.title: Amazon security research reportedly led to the White House's Anthropic Fable ban
further_links.summary: Amazon's internal security research is reported to have been the trigger for the White House ordering Anthropic to cut off access to its Fable and Mythos AI models.

further_links.title: The future of Hollywood isn't feeding prompts into vanilla gen AI models
further_links.summary: At Tribeca 2026, filmmakers and AI developers including those from Google DeepMind and OpenAI discussed how serious creative AI use goes far beyond simple prompt-based generation.

further_links.title: Meta Employees Absolutely Hate Mark Zuckerberg's Plan for a Companywide AI Hackathon [Metered]
further_links.summary: Meta employees have reportedly pushed back strongly against Mark Zuckerberg's proposal for a company-wide AI hackathon, citing concerns about workload and the initiative's framing.

further_links.title: Apple's Camera Chief Thinks AI Can Give You Superpowers [Metered]
further_links.summary: Apple's head of camera software discusses how AI-powered photo and video tools are being designed to extend human creative capability rather than replace it.

further_links.title: Apple's new AI photo editing tools mostly work, for better and worse
further_links.summary: The Verge offers a hands-on assessment of Apple's latest AI-powered photo editing features, finding them functional but inconsistent in practice.

further_links.title: Siri is good now??
further_links.summary: The Verge podcast examines whether Apple's revamped Siri has meaningfully improved as an AI assistant following recent updates.

further_links.title: Oracle wades into outcome-based AI billing waters
further_links.summary: Oracle is reportedly moving toward outcome-based pricing for its AI services, a shift that could influence how enterprise AI products are commercially structured.

further_links.title: China Didn't Make Americans Hate Data Centers [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired investigates the domestic roots of US public opposition to data centre expansion, finding that local concerns — not geopolitical anxieties about China — are the primary driver.
